quotes_used_verbatim: When you book a shore excursion through Royal Caribbean, we guarantee that if your tour is delayed, the ship will wait for you.
In the unlikely event that your tour is significantly delayed, and the ship cannot wait, we will make all the arrangements for you to return to the ship at no expense to you.
The ship will not wait for any guest faring on their own, as it is their responsibility to be onboard before the ship's scheduled departure time.
primary_sources.attribution_discipline: Quoted AS Royal Caribbean's wording and explicitly labelled in the article as one line's terms, with the reader told to check their own line rather than assume this sentence covers them.

primary_sources.source: Carnival, Princess and Norwegian shore-excursion terms
primary_sources.substance_used: That these lines describe themselves in excursion terms as arranging services supplied by independent operators and limit their liability for the excursion itself.
primary_sources.care_note: Characterised in general terms only; no verbatim quotation and no specific clause is attributed to a named line, because those pages were surfaced in search but not individually fetched and quoted.

claims.verification_correction_recorded: An earlier search summary attributed missed-ship policy to a Royal Caribbean page about CANCELLING a cruise. That page was fetched and did NOT contain the policy - it covers refunds on cancellation. The correct page was located and fetched before anything was published. Recorded because it is exactly the failure mode of trusting search summaries.
claims.not_claimed: NO claim that all lines guarantee to wait; NO all-aboard time figures; NO claim about what any insurance policy covers (the reader is told to check); NO claim about port agent procedures beyond that an agent exists and their details appear on the daily programme; NO cost figures for rejoining a ship.
claims.editorial: The risk-varies-by-port framing, the buy-back-a-margin advice and the guarantee-is-logistics-not-tour-quality distinction are the site's own reasoning.

voice_audit.audited_against: voice-audit v2.3.0 (full Six-Axis Scan + AI-Authorship Cluster Detection), like-a-human v3.2.0, emotional-hook-test v2.0.0, publication-proofreader v1.0.0
voice_audit.audited_by: Claude (patron syl), operator-requested full voice-skill pass
voice_audit.audit_scope: full article body (itemprop=articleBody) — not the description or ai-summary
voice_audit.supersedes: An earlier partial attestation written 2026-09-05 that covered only part of Axis 1 and some cadence measurement. It did not carry must_be_present, cluster_detection or risk_rating, and it was therefore NOT schema-conformant to the skill. This block replaces it.

machine_tells._note: All counts are post-correction. Intensifiers surviving the scan were each tested by deletion per v2.3.0 sharpening: those that change meaning ('genuinely' meaning actually/seriously) were kept; those that were rhetorical padding were cut.

must_be_present.first_person_attestation_with_date: 1, added during this audit: the near-miss where the top search result pointed at a Royal Caribbean page about cancellations rather than missed ships, caught before quoting. Reader-serving friction, not lived attestation; no travel date. Colophon escape applies.
must_be_present.honest_limitation_acknowledged: Explicit: the article states the guarantee covers logistics, not tour quality or safety, and declines to extend it.
must_be_present.from_the_pier_specificity: n/a — not a port or ship page
must_be_present.named_real_specifics: Named organisations and named source documents throughout (see primary_sources). No named private individual, by design — the site does not name passengers or crew without cause.

cadence._measurement_limit: The short-sentence counter splits on [.!?] followed by whitespace and therefore MERGES a short sentence that follows a closing quotation mark. It under-counts. Verified by hand on cruise-single-supplement-explained, where 'Two hundred percent.' is present in the body but was not counted.

cluster_detection.layer_1_notes: No semantic placeholders, no broad authority claims without anchors, no rhythm-only triplet closures, no cross-entity feature blending. The clean-linear-arc signal was checked and does not hold: each page carries at least one admitted limit or refusal.
cluster_detection.layer_3_notes: A contradiction-with-public-source-expectation note (the search result was wrong); admitted authorial near-error; bounded scope on what the guarantee does not buy.

voice_audit.honest_limit: This attestation records a mechanical scan plus the auditor's judgment on each hit. It measures the presence of known tells, structural variance, and signal clustering. It cannot certify that the prose reads as lived experience to a human reader, and on six of these seven pages it does not claim to — those pages are sourced research and say so.

voice_audit_batch_findings.sourcing_violation_found_and_fixed: cruise-single-supplement-explained closed with 'Purpose-built solo cabins barely existed fifteen years ago and now run to the high hundreds across one line's fleet alone.' Neither the count nor the history was sourced; no solo-cabin count was ever fetched. It also directly contradicted this article's own claims.not_claimed field ('NO claim about the number of solo cabins on any ship or in any fleet'). The closing was rewritten to keep only what the NCL page supports and to say plainly that the count is not knowable from here. Found by the cluster-detection Layer 1 check for broad authority claims without specifics, NOT by any validator or by the earlier partial audit.
voice_audit_batch_findings.unverified_regulation_softened: cruise-muster-drill-explained asserted 'Behind the line's own policy sits international maritime regulation requiring a muster for embarking passengers around departure' as flat fact, while its sidecar recorded that no regulatory text had been fetched. The body now states the limit in the reader's view and warns against quoting a citation from the page.
voice_audit_batch_findings.authorial_presence_added: how-to-read-a-cdc-cruise-inspection-score, cruise-what-if-you-miss-the-ship and cruise-muster-drill-explained had ZERO first-person presence of any kind — the exact absence pattern behind the Anthem June 2026 reader-feedback failure. One true authorial paragraph was added to each, reporting something that actually happened during research. No lived experience was manufactured.
voice_audit_batch_findings.word_level_corrections: CDC: 'CDC maintains' to 'CDC runs' (copulative avoidance); 'than the hospitality industry offers' to 'manages' (promotional verb); 'a genuinely good instrument' to 'a good instrument' (intensifier padding). Muster: 'genuinely useful knowledge' to 'useful knowledge'. Single supplement: 'NCL offers purpose-built solo accommodation' to 'has'; 'what compensation the line offers' to 'gives'. Medical: 'the sentence most people find out too late' rewritten to remove an unsourced generalisation about readers.
voice_audit_batch_findings.typography_findings: External source links lacked target=_blank against the corpus convention; added on 5 pages (the buymeacoffee CTA keeps its own house form). Two proofreader flags were the AUDITOR's error, not the articles': the double-space-after-period hits were an artifact of replacing HTML tags with spaces (zero double spaces exist in the raw markup), and the curly-quote check contradicts the site's actual practice — four published articles carry zero curly quotes and 2 to 38 straight apostrophes each, so these seven match the corpus and were deliberately not churned. That contradiction between publication-proofreader v1.0.0 and the corpus needs an operator decision.
voice_audit_batch_findings.false_positives_recorded: 'a must' in cruise-muster-drill-explained matches inside the word 'muster'; 'when it comes to' in the same article sits inside a verbatim Royal Caribbean quotation and cannot be altered.
